# limpet

> A single-file, pure-bash macOS CLI that lets you run your Mac off an external SSD as **primary storage** — and keeps working the instant the drive is unplugged. It fails over to a real local folder within a second, then merges your offline work back onto the drive when it returns, never overwriting on a clash.

limpet exists because Macs ship with small, expensive internal storage. Many people move Documents, Downloads, Desktop, and project folders onto a cheap external SSD and symlink to it — which breaks the moment the drive is unplugged (saves fail, folders look empty, reboots split files across two places). macOS has no built-in "work offline, sync when it's back" mechanism for external volumes (the way Windows has Offline Files). limpet is that missing mechanism.

## How it works
- **Connected:** your folders are symlinks straight to the drive — zero overhead, full speed.
- **Unplugged:** a launchd guard (WatchPaths /Volumes) turns each symlink back into a real local folder within a second, so every save keeps working.
- **Reconnected:** a throttled terminal-shell hook copies whatever you made offline back onto the drive, keeping BOTH copies on any name clash (`name.local-<timestamp>`) — it never overwrites.

The split exists because macOS security (TCC) blocks background/launchd processes from writing to external volumes; the guard only does local symlink swaps (no Full Disk Access needed), and the terminal hook does the merge-back that must touch the drive.

## Safety
- Verified copy before delete: `ditto` copy, then a byte-level shasum manifest is verified before the original is removed. If verification fails, the original is left untouched.
- Never overwrites on merge (keep-both, timestamped).
- No kernel extensions, no daemons, no network (except an optional daily update check). ~300 lines of readable bash.
- Not a backup — it keeps data available and unplug-resilient; keep Time Machine too.

## Install
```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/notpritam/limpet/main/install.sh | bash
limpet setup      # interactive: pick a drive + folders
limpet status
```

## Key commands
- `limpet setup` — interactive wizard (also scriptable: `--drive`, `--folders`, `--yes`).
- `limpet status [--json]` — drive + folder state.
- `limpet link <path>` / `limpet unlink <path>` — move any extra file/folder onto the drive and back.
- `limpet list` — managed folders + ad-hoc links.
- `limpet doctor` — health-check and offer fixes.
- `limpet sync` — run failover/failback + mirror now.
- `limpet update [--check]` — self-update from GitHub Releases (syntax-checked before replacing the binary).
- `limpet uninstall` — remove guard + hook, optionally restore folders locally.

## Facts
- Platform: macOS only (relies on launchd, ditto, APFS).
- Language: pure bash, POSIX/bash-3.2 safe, single file.
- License: MIT © Pritam Sharma.
- Author: Pritam Sharma (https://www.notpritam.in/).
- Made as a personal project and published so others with the same "big Mac, small disk, cheap external SSD" setup can use it.
